title: 1700–1706 Prairie under one roof
items: The two Glessner townhouses at 1700 and 1706 Prairie had separate roofs, each hipped down at the party line, so the roofs crossed in a valley with a brick slab standing out of it. They now share one mansard, as both period photographs show. The party wall sits on the line between the houses and runs up through the roof, its pale coping following the slope from the cornice to the deck.
One chimney stands on the party wall just behind the railing, and another stands on 1700's north end wall. A single downpipe runs down the front on the party line.
The rooftop railing is now the white fret from the photographs: square posts, one bar corner to corner in each panel, and a squared key in each triangle. It replaces the iron-style cresting.
